'''Tatiana Birshtein''' or '''Tat'yana Maksimovna Birshtein''' ([[Russian Language|Russian]]: Татья́на Макси́мовна Бирште́йн, 20 December 1928 – 23 February 2022) was a Russian molecular scientist. Birshtein specialised in the physics of polymers. In 2007 she was given the [[L'Oréal-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science|L'Oréal-UNESCO Award for Women in Science]].

==Life and career==
Birshtein was born in Leningrad (now [[Saint Petersburg]]) in 1928. She survived [[Siege of Leningrad]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Воспоминания Татьяны Максимовны Бирштейн о войне |url=https://macro.ru/2023/05/vospominaniya-tatyany-maksimovny-birshtejn-o-vojne/}}</ref> She attended [[Leningrad State University]].<ref name=birthday>[http://imc.macro.ru:8080/web/guest/birshtein Tat'yana Maksimovna Birshtein] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180405163620/http://imc.macro.ru:8080/web/guest/birshtein |date=2018-04-05 }}, www.imc.macro.ru, Retrieved 16 November 2015</ref>

Birshtein specialised in the theoretical physics of polymers in Saint Petersburg at the Institute of Macromolecular Compounds of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]]. This institution had been created as part of Professor [[Mikhail Volkenstein]]'s 1950s Leningrad school of polymer science. The institution was synonymous with Birshtein and she is said to have dedicated her life to science.<ref name=birthday/>

She has published extensively on polymers,<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/ma00001a023| title= Coil-globule type transitions in polymers. 1. Collapse of layers of grafted polymer chains| year= 1991| last1= Zhulina| first1= E. B.| last2= Borisov| first2= O. V.| last3= Pryamitsyn| first3= V. A.| last4= Birshtein| first4= T. M.| journal=[[Macromolecules]]| volume= 24| issue= 1| pages= 140–149| bibcode= 1991MaMol..24..140Z}}</ref> DNA stability,<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1002/bip.1969.360080502| title= Determination of stability of the DNA double helix in an aqueous medium| year= 1969| last1= Privalov| first1= P. L.| last2= Ptitsyn| first2= O. B.| last3= Birshtein| first3= T. M.| journal=[[Biopolymers (journal)|Biopolymers]]| volume= 8| issue= 5| pages= 559–571| s2cid= 83732243}}</ref> micelle structure,<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1016/0032-3861(89)90399-6| title= Scaling theory of supermolecular structures in block copolymer-solvent systems: 1. Model of micellar structures| year= 1989| last1= Birshtein| first1= T.M.| last2= Zhulina| first2= E.B.| journal= Polymer| volume= 30| pages= 170–177}}</ref> as well as structures of organic molecules.<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1016/0022-2860(75)85131-3| title= The theoretical conformational analysis of some bridged aromatic compounds: Diphenyl ether, diphenylmethane, benzophenone and diphenyl sulphide| year= 1975| last1= Zubkov| first1= V.A.| last2= Birshtein| first2= T.M.| last3= Milevskaya| first3= I.S.| journal=[[Journal of Molecular Structure]]| volume= 27| issue= 1| pages= 139–149| bibcode= 1975JMoSt..27..139Z}}</ref>

On 22 February 2007, she was awarded $100,000, when she was given the [[L'Oréal-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science|L'Oréal-UNESCO Award for Women in Science]]. The award was for her "contribution to the understanding of the shapes, sizes and motions of large molecules".<ref name="unesco-2007">{{cite web| publisher = UNESCOPRESS| date = 2007-03-02| title = Five outstanding women scientists receive L'Oréal-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science 2007| url = http://portal.unesco.org/science/en/ev.php-URL_ID=5212&URL_DO=DO_TOPIC&URL_SECTION=201.html| accessdate = 2015-11-16| url-status = dead| archiveurl = http://webarchive.loc.gov/all/20150412060238/http://portal.unesco.org/science/en/ev.php-URL_ID=5212&URL_DO=DO_TOPIC&URL_SECTION=201.html| archivedate =2015-04-12| website=Library of Congress Web Archives}}</ref>

Birshtein died on 23 February 2022, at the age of 93.<ref>{{cite web | title=Saying goodbye to Tat'yana Maksimovna Birshtein | website=Macro.ru | date= | url=https://macro.ru/2022/02/proshhaemsya-s-tatyanoj-maksimovnoj-birshtejn/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220224203111/https://macro.ru/2022/02/proshhaemsya-s-tatyanoj-maksimovnoj-birshtejn/ | archive-date=February 24, 2022 | url-status=live }}</ref>

== Awards ==

* [[Medal "For the Defence of Leningrad"]] (1944)
* [[Honoured Scientist of the Russian Federation]] (1998)
* Award named after V. A. Kargin RAS (2008)
